outcome: persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN)
cohort: Preterm infants born between 22 and 31 weeks of gestation and weighing <= 1500 g in Japan between 2003 and 2017.
finding: Maternal hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) were associated with higher odds of respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) but reduced odds of persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN), while risks for chronic lung disease, home oxygen therapy, and medium-term respiratory outcomes were comparable to the non-HDP group.
